newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - April 17.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Fay Richwhite tries to gag Winebox inquiry: Fay Richwhite and Co has mounted a High Court challenge to prevent the Cook Islands tax commission of inquiry from deciding or reporting on the Winebox documents. Page 1.

Peters criticised by super taskforce member: Treasurer Winston Peters drew sharp criticism on Wednesday from Todd Superannuation Taskforce member Michael Littlewood, as well as National, Labour and Alliance MPs, for his latest disclosures on the proposed compulsory superannuation scheme. Page 1.

Super scheme will get less affordable, says firm chief: The present superannuation scheme is affordable, though it will become "less affordable" in the future, according to Jacques Martin New Zealand's chief executive, Peter Baynes. Page 2.

Forestry backlash predicted: The New Zealand Farm Forestry Association has warned the government of a backlash if the proposed compulsory superannuation does not exclude privately owned woodlots. Page 2.
Truancy service failing -- Mallard: The government's truancy service had failed to find 484 children who should have been enrolled at school, Labour MP Trevor Mallard said on Wednesday. Page 2.

Tasks for job seekers suggested: Simple household repairs and maintenance for low-income earners or beneficiaries could be done by job seekers earning the community wage, Employment Minister Peter McCardle said on Wednesday. Page 2.
Latimer's plans for Maori party won't work -- elder: Sir Graham Latimer's plans for a new Maori party won't get the support of Maori voters, Wellington elder Bill Katene says. Page 2.
Time for NZ to train with US troops -- PM: The time had come for the New Zealand military to be able to train with American defence troops, Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Wednesday. Page 2.
Better treatment too late -- haemophiliacs: Haemophiliacs said a government announcement on Wednesday of better treatment for them was probably too little and too late. Page 2.

Free visits to doctor confirmed: Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton says the coalition's commitment to free doctors' visits and prescription charges for children under the age of six will start from July 1 and be paid for out of this budget round. Page 2.
Wellington cafe culture stays ahead of the rest: Cafe Culture continues to thrive in Wellington, keeping well ahead of the rest of New Zealand in sales. Page 17.
Goodman Fielder to bid again for Defiance: Goodman Fielder is likely to propose a partial sell-off of Defiance Food Insudtries assets in a new bid to buy the Christchurch-based company. Page 17.
Countrywide cuts floating mortgage rate: Countrywide Bank cut its floating mortgage rate from 9.95 percent to 9.4 percent on Wednesday, citing Tuesday's low inflation figure. Page 17.
Birch rejects criticism of plans to spend more: Finance Minister Bill Birch has rejected criticism by National Bank chief economist Adrian Orr of the government's spending. Page 17.
Infratil considers share rights issue: Infrastructure and Utilities shareholders may be offered shares in a new company, Infratil International. Page 17.

Simpler reporting for most companies: About 90 percent of companies will qualify for a simpler regime of "differential reporting" after reporting changes were approved by the Institute of Chartered Accountants. Page 17.

Taranaki methanol output rises: Methanex increased its Taranaki methanol production to 549,000 tonnes in the March quarter, from 357,000 tonnes in March 1996, as international prices rose due to a combination of increased demand and outages at competitors' plants. Page 17.

Dividend for Donaghys: Shareholders in diversified industrial group Donaghys stand to gain a special dividend of 42 cents a share from the splitting off of Scott Technology as a separately listed company. Page 17.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Consumers spend less on higher-priced items: New Zealanders spend $107 million less on retail goods and services in February than at the same time in 1996, figures released on Wednesday by Statistics New Zealand show.

Macraes Mining moves quickly: Gold producer Macraes Mining is urgently seeking planning consent for the $120 million expansion of its Central Otago gold quarry, just as negative publicity about the mining industry's control of toxic waste raises the possibility of more stringent mining laws.

Results from East Coast site encourage Enerco: Gas company Enerco New Zealand is likely to proceed with further testing of its oil and gas exploration prospect on the East Coast of the North Island following encouraging results from an initial survey.

Phillips' staff share scheme deal disclosed: Former Pacer Kerridge Corporation chairman David Phillips collected more than $400,000 of interest on a share sale credit, plus dividends on the shares, presecutor Lyn Stevens told Phillips' fraud and
perjury trial on Wednesday.
Kiwi continues to fall: The New Zealand dollar and yields on longer term government stock continued to fall on Wednesday.
THE PRESS

Broadside for compulsory super: The government found few fans for its compulsory superannuation scheme on Wednesday, with Opposition parties declaring it would cost billions and a high-profile Cabinet member airing doubts. Page 1.

Defiance family split as Bunge increases offer: A higher bid for Australia's Defiance Mills seems to have split apart the company's controlling family, while preference shareholders in Christchurch-based Defiance Food Industries have also been offered more. Page 27.
South Island retail sales down 3.6 percent: South Island retail sales fell 3.6 percent in February compared with February last year. Canterbury regional sales fell 3.2 percent. Page 27.
WestpacTrust to close southern branches: WestpacTrust announced on Wednesday that it will close 13 bank branches in Otago and Southland. Page 27.

Firestone plans firm up: In the expectation that appropriate co-operative agreements are reached, Firestone NZ is looking to start its seven-day continuous production of its Christchurch plant in August. Page 27.
-- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
